title: The Security Manager and JDK internals after Java 17

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Per this page, what happens since Java 18 when code calls `System.setSecurityManager(...)` at run time?

options.text: The call installs it and the JVM logs a warning
options.says: The page says that since Java 18 a Security Manager cannot be installed at run time without the allow setting, so it is not installed with a warning.

options.text: The call installs it once a policy file is set
options.says: The page names one condition only: the JVM must be started with -Djava.security.manager=allow; a policy file does not lift the ban.

options.text: The call throws unless a startup flag allows it
options.says: The page says that since Java 18 a Security Manager cannot be installed at run time unless the JVM was started with -Djava.security.manager=allow.

origin.section: Q2: Why was the Security Manager deprecated in Java 17?

questions.stem: A library still reflects into a JDK-internal package on Java 17. Per this page, how is that access granted?

options.text: With --illegal-access=permit given on the command line
options.says: The page says Java 17 removed --illegal-access entirely, so that option no longer exists.

options.text: With --add-opens given on the command line or in the manifest
options.says: The page's migration strategy is --add-opens on the command line, or the Add-Opens attribute in an executable JAR's manifest.

options.text: With an opens clause written in the app's module-info.java
options.says: The page says module-info.java cannot open another module's packages, so the JDK's packages cannot be opened there.

origin.section: Q4: How does Java 17 handle strong encapsulation of JDK internals?

concepts: The Security Manager is deprecated for removal, and since Java 18 installing one fails unless the JVM allows it with -Djava.security.manager=allow.
Java 17 removed --illegal-access, so reflective access to JDK internals needs --add-opens on the command line or in the JAR manifest.
